newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Vanstone says jobs data on f'cast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Vanstone says jobs data on f'cast.

text.p: Australian Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone said on Thursday that employment data released earlier by the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed the government's forecasts for employment were well on track.
"I think these figures show that we're well on track," Vanstone told reporters when asked if the latest figures were consistent with the budget forecasts.

The government has forecast average employment growth of 1.5 percent for the 1996/97 year and a 2.0 percent rise in employment between the June quarter in 1996 and the June quarter in 1997. It has forecast an average unemployment rate of 8.5 percent for the 1996/97 year and an average of 8.25 percent unemployment for the June quarter in 1997.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics said its seasonally adjusted estimate of the number of employed persons rose 24,400 in November to 8.40 million, against 8.37 million in October and 8.33 million a year earlier. The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate fell to 8.5 percent in November from 8.8 percent in October, compared with 8.5 percent in November 1995.

Vanstone also said it would take some time for the benefits of Wednesday's interest rate cut and the partial privatisation of telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp to flow through to the labour market.
"It will take some time for the benefit of those things to flow through," she said.
Economists had expected employment to rise around 10,000 in November, seasonally adjusted, with the unemployment rate easing to 8.7 percent.
